page: Amazon Web Services m3.2xlarge is a legacy general-purpose instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor built on x86_64 architecture. Virtualized via Xen, the instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and a shared 25 MB L3 cache. Memory allocation totals 30.0 GB of RAM, equating to 3.75 GB per vCPU. The instance comes equipped with 160 GB of local SSD storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, with zero included GPUs.

Benchmark measurements reflect the generational limitations of the Ivy Bridge architecture. Single-core throughput ranks in lower brackets, demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 710.0 and a stress-ng single-core metric of 1279.49. Multi-threaded execution performs moderately better, yielding an average PassMark CPU score of 7144.84 and a Clang compilation score of 6333.0. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth achieves 49.24 GB/sec while write operations achieve 35.54 GB/sec, positioning general memory throughput in the middle tier.

Instruction set support includes AVX and AES-NI, but excludes newer instruction sets such as AVX-512, AMX, and SHA extensions. As a consequence, complex vector calculations and advanced machine learning routines show low throughput, as seen in an inference generation speed of 5.26 tokens per second on a medium 7B model.

The presence of 160 GB integrated local SSD storage provides fast temporary disk I/O without requiring external block volumes. However, older generation CPU cores offer reduced efficiency per unit of resource compared to modern hardware iterations. Amazon Web Services m3.2xlarge is best suited for legacy application hosting, moderate web serving, basic batch jobs, and development environments that require a balanced memory profile and scratch disk space.
description: Amazon Web Services m3.2xlarge is an older-generation general-purpose instance featuring 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores on an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The configuration delivers 30.0 GB of memory, or 3.75 GB per vCPU, alongside 160 GB of bundled local SSD storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance lacks hardware acceleration and modern vector instruction sets like AVX-512. Benchmark results reflect low single-core performance alongside average multi-core and memory subsystem throughput, reaching a PassMark CPU score of 7144.84 and static web serving throughput of 6.7 GB/sec. Due to its balanced vCPU-to-memory allocation and integrated local SSD scratch space, the m3.2xlarge is suitable for legacy multi-threaded services, development testing, and baseline web application hosting.
